memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: For forty days the flood kept coming on the earth, and as the waters increased they lifted the ark high above the earth. The waters rose and increased greatly on the earth, and the ark floated on the surface of the water. - Gen 7:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very waters that destroyed the world lifted the ark to safety. As the flood rose higher and higher, it did not sink Noah - it carried him. The same waters that meant death for the disobedient meant deliverance for those inside the ark. What drowned the world bore up God's people.

There is a profound truth hidden here. The very thing that seems overwhelming - the rising tide of trouble - can, in God's hands, become the means of lifting us higher. Noah did not escape the flood by avoiding the waters; he was carried through them, held up by God's provision in the midst of them.

We often pray for God to remove the floods from our lives. But sometimes God does not take away the waters; instead He gives us an ark and lets the very trials that could sink us lift us closer to Him. The storms that would destroy us become, by grace, the storms that draw us upward.

This is the promise God gives His people: "When you pass through the waters, I will be with you... they will not sweep over you" (Isa 43:2). Notice - not "if" but "when," and not "around" but "through." In Christ, the floods of life cannot drown us; held safe in Him, we are lifted through them. What threatens to sink you may be the very thing God uses to raise you higher.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you asking God to remove your floods, or to carry you through them?
- How might God be using a hard season to lift you closer to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when the waters rise in my life, help me trust that in Christ they cannot drown me. Carry me through the floods, and use even my trials to lift me closer to You.
